Author: Rakesh Thapliyal
Bench: Rakesh Thapliyal
Sl. Office Notes,
No. Date reports,
 orders or Court'S Or Judge'S Order

S  proceedings  or directions  and  Registrar's  order with  Signatures  ABA No. 1239 of 2025  Hon'ble Rakesh Thapliyal, J.
1.
Mr. Yogesh Pant, learned counsel for the applicant.
2. Ms. Meenakshi Sharma, learned Brief Holder for the State.

3. The instant anticipatory bail application has been moved by the applicant Smt. Vimla Devi, W/o Late Satish Singh and Anju @ Anjali, D/o Late Satish Singh praying for anticipatory bail in reference to FIR dated 25.10.2025, bearing FIR No. 306 of 205, registered at P.S. Khatima District U.S. Nagar,
wherein both the applicants along with one Akash, who is in fact son of applicant no. 1, have been implicated for the offences punishable under Sections 376, 420 IPC and 115(2) of BNS 2023.

4. Learned counsel for the applicant argued that the FIR has been registered on an application moved by the complainant under Section 175(3) of BNSS 2023 with the allegations that she engaged with one Akash who shown himself to be an employee of S.S.B. but as a matter of fact he is not the employee of S.S.B., and after engagement on various occasions he demanded money which the complainant fulfilled and during this period on various occasions Akash committed sexual assault with the complainant.

5. Learned counsel for the applicant argued that both the applicants are innocent, and even on perusal of the FIR there is no allegation against the applicants and whatever be the allegations have been alleged that is against Akash and admittedly both the complainant and Akash were engaged but due to some differences in between both of them the FIR has been lodged.

He further submits that the FIR reveals that the main accused is Akash and the present applicants have no role and Akash has already been arrested and is in jail, however, since, both the applicants are named in the FIR, therefore, there is an apprehension of arrest.

6. Ms. Meenakshi Sharma, learned Brief Holder for the State prays for and is granted four weeks'
time to file counter affidavit.

Two weeks thereafter is granted to the applicant to file rejoinder ABA/1239/2025 on 4 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/82565248/
1 affidavit.
7.
8. List this case in the first week of March 2026.

(Rakesh Thapliyal, J.) 04.12.2025 Parul ABA/1239/2025 on 4 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/82565248/

opennyai_summary.decision:
Two weeks thereafter is granted to the applicant to file rejoinder ABA/1239/2025 on 4 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/82565248/
1 affidavit.
7.
Having heard the arguments of learned counsel for the parties, for an interim measure, and taking into consideration that the main accused is Akash and present applicants are mother and sister of Akash, this Court is of the view that both the applicants deserves for interim protection, and, as such, without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, in an event of arrest during investigation, both the applicants shall be released on interim anticipatory bail subject to furnishing of personal bond with two reliable sureties, each of the like amount, to the satisfaction of the arresting Officer subject to the following conditions:-
(i) The applicants shall cooperate with the investigation;
(ii) The applicants shall not approach any witness in any manner, whatsoever.
8. List this case in the first week of March 2026.
